porch_floor_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net porch/patio floor area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours. Dual-substrate spec — concrete and wood substrates branch at task selection, not at modifier level.

task_production_rates.name: Mobilization and Equipment Staging
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Load truck with floor-specific equipment: roller frames, extension poles, mixing paddle, concrete prep tools (grinder or etch supplies), moisture meter, anti-slip aggregate. 45 min baseline includes drive time and unload. Fixed regardless of floor area.

defect_tolerance.all: All required tools and materials staged at work area before task start.

task_production_rates.name: Area Preparation — Furniture and Obstacle Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove or relocate porch/patio furniture, planters, rugs, doormats, and loose items. Stage in garage or yard away from work zone. 60 min baseline for typical 200-400 SF porch. Larger patios with extensive furnishing trend toward 90 min. Fixed time — not area-dependent.

defect_tolerance.all: All moveable items cleared from work surface. Owner-retained items documented and protected in place.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Base Protection — Masking at Porch-to-House Junction
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply 2-3" painter's tape along house wall at floor junction, attach 12-18" plastic sheeting above tape line to protect siding/brick. ~30 sec per LF. LF of house wall along porch edge. Identical pattern to deck siding protection.

defect_tolerance.all: Continuous tape line at wall-floor junction. Sheeting secured with no gaps. No coating contact on wall surface.

task_production_rates.name: Railing Base Protection — Masking at Post and Picket Bases
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask around railing post bases and picket bottoms with tape and small plastic sections. Slower than wall base due to multiple small areas around posts. ~36 sec per LF. LF of railing run.

defect_tolerance.all: All post bases and picket bottoms masked. No coating bridging onto railing surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Door Threshold Protection — Masking Entry Transitions
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask door threshold and weatherstrip with tape, apply temporary plastic barrier to prevent tracking. ~12 min per EA. Includes tape application, plastic drape, and temporary 'wet floor' barrier setup. Critical for occupied homes.

defect_tolerance.all: Threshold fully masked. No coating on weatherstrip or door bottom. Barrier in place during cure.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection — Perimeter Plantings
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along porch perimeter where landscape beds are adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Prevents acid etch runoff or coating drips from contacting plantings. Secure against wind.

defect_tolerance.all: Full perimeter coverage of adjacent plantings. Secure against wind. No chemical runoff onto vegetation.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection — Adjacent Walks and Drives
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask adjacent walkways, driveways, and hardscape at porch edge transition. Tape edge line plus 24-36" plastic sheeting or paper. ~30 sec per LF. Prevents coating overflow at porch edge.

defect_tolerance.all: Clean edge line at porch-to-hardscape transition. No coating on adjacent surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Moisture Test — Calcium Chloride or RH Probe
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Set up calcium chloride test kit or RH probe per ASTM F1869/F2170. ~40 min per test EA includes surface prep, kit placement, documentation. Results require 60-72 hr — scheduling item, not continuous labor. Typically 1 test per 500 SF, minimum 3 per project. Concrete substrate only.

defect_tolerance.all: Test performed per ASTM protocol. Results documented with timestamp and location. Proceed only if moisture < 3 lbs/1000 SF/24hr (calcium chloride) or < 75% RH (probe).

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Acid Etch — Profile and Clean Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply muriatic or phosphoric acid solution, scrub with stiff broom, neutralize, rinse. 300 SF/hr single worker. Manual labor-intensive process. Creates CSP 2-3 profile for coating adhesion. Includes mixing, application, dwell, scrub, neutralize, and rinse. Appropriate for porch enamel and acrylic sealer systems.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform etch profile across entire surface. Water drops absorb within 30 sec (break test passes). No glossy/sealed areas remaining. Neutralization verified with pH test strip (pH 7-9).

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Diamond Grind — Mechanical Surface Profiling
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk-behind diamond grinder creates CSP 3-5 profile. 700 SF/hr with equipment. Equipment-assisted — significantly faster than acid etch. Required for polyurea systems and preferred for high-build coatings. Includes equipment setup, grinding passes, and vacuum dust collection.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform grind profile across entire surface. No high spots or glossy patches remaining. Dust vacuumed — no residual slurry. Profile verified per ICRI CSP comparator chip.

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Crack Fill and Patch
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Route, clean, and fill cracks with flexible polyurethane or epoxy filler. 30 LF/hr baseline for hairline to 1/4" cracks. Wider cracks or spalled areas significantly slower. Includes crack routing (if needed), vacuuming debris, filler application, and feathering. LF from field measure.

defect_tolerance.all: Cracks filled flush to surrounding surface. No voids or shrinkage. Feathered edges blend with floor plane. Structural cracks flagged — cosmetic fill only (not structural repair).

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Surface Clean — Degrease and Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash or scrub with TSP/degreaser solution. 500 SF/hr baseline. Removes dirt, oil, efflorescence, mildew, and loose material. Includes detergent application, dwell time, scrub/pressure wash, and rinse. Must dry 24-48 hr before coating. Concrete substrate only.

defect_tolerance.all: Surface visibly clean — no oil stains, mildew, or efflorescence. Water breaks evenly across surface (no beading from contaminants). Dry to touch before coating.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Mill Glaze Removal — Coarse Sand
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Belt or orbital sander with 60-80 grit to remove mill glaze from new wood porch flooring. 50 SF/hr single worker. Slow process — must break through glazed surface for primer adhesion without gouging. Includes sanding, vacuuming dust, and tack cloth wipe. Wood substrate, new condition only.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform dull surface — no glossy mill glaze patches remaining. No gouges, cross-grain scratches, or over-sanding. Dust removed before priming.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Moisture Content Test
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter reading at multiple points across wood porch floor. ~20 min per test zone EA. Includes calibration check, multi-point readings, and documentation. Proceed only if MC < 15% for oil-based, < 18% for water-based coatings. Wood substrate only.

defect_tolerance.all: MC readings documented with location map. All zones below threshold for selected coating system. High readings flagged — extend dry time or investigate moisture source.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Floor Sand — Surface Preparation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Orbital sander with 80-100 grit for general surface prep on wood porch floor. 70 SF/hr single worker. Creates tooth for primer adhesion. Includes sanding with the grain, vacuuming, and tack cloth wipe. Slightly faster than mill glaze removal because surface is already open.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform scratch pattern with the grain. No glossy areas remaining. No cross-grain scratches. All dust removed.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Floor Clean — Wash and Prep
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Low-pressure wash or scrub with deck cleaner to remove dirt, mildew, and sanding dust. 500 SF/hr baseline. Low pressure only (< 1500 PSI) to avoid wood fiber damage. Includes detergent application, light scrub, rinse. Dry 24-48 hr before priming. Wood substrate only.

defect_tolerance.all: Surface clean and free of contaminants. No raised grain from excessive pressure. Dry before primer application.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll alkali-resistant primer on concrete floor with 3/8-1/2" nap roller on extension pole. 200 SF/hr single worker. Includes cutting in at edges with brush (~15% of time) and rolling field. Primer blocks alkali migration and provides adhesion base for porch enamel or acrylic sealer.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete uniform coverage — no holidays, thin spots, or puddles. Brush-cut edges feathered into roll field. Dry film build per product TDS.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer — Spray + Backroll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer onto concrete floor, immediately backroll with 3/8" nap. 375 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Spray provides speed and even coverage, backroll ensures penetration into surface profile. Efficient on larger porches (>300 SF). Requires overspray containment.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete uniform coverage. Backroll ensures primer penetrates surface profile. No overspray on adjacent surfaces. Even wet film build.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Floor Primer — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll exterior wood primer (alkyd or acrylic bonding primer) on wood porch floor with 3/8" nap roller on extension pole. 200 SF/hr single worker. Includes cutting in at edges and around post bases. Primer seals wood grain and provides adhesion base for porch enamel.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete coverage — no bare wood visible. Even film build. No puddles in board gaps. Brush-cut edges feathered into roll field.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Floor Primer — Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush primer into wood porch floor boards — used for small porches or detailed areas around posts, steps, and edges. 100 SF/hr single worker. Brush works primer into wood grain and board gaps. Slower than roll but better penetration into narrow boards and tongue-and-groove joints.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete coverage including board edges and gaps. Even film build. No drips or puddles.

task_production_rates.name: Polyurea Primer — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll polyurea-compatible primer/basecoat on diamond-ground concrete. 250 SF/hr single worker. Fast-cure chemistry — must work in manageable sections. Short pot life requires efficient technique. Includes mixing component A+B and rolling in continuous passes.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete coverage within pot life window. Even film build. No bare spots or thin areas. Mixed and applied per manufacturer ratio specifications.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture-Mitigating Primer — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll moisture-mitigating epoxy primer on concrete with elevated moisture readings. 175 SF/hr single worker. Two-component epoxy — mix, apply within pot life, maintain wet edge. Slower than standard primer due to component mixing and limited working time. Required when moisture test indicates 3-5 lbs/1000 SF/24hr.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete pinhole-free coverage. Mixed at correct ratio. Applied within pot life. No fisheyes or bare spots. Verify film thickness with wet mil gauge.

task_production_rates.name: Porch & Floor Enamel — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll porch and floor enamel (alkyd or latex) with 3/8-3/4" nap roller on extension pole. 200 SF/hr single worker on concrete. Includes cutting in edges with brush (~15% of time). Enamel is thicker-body than wall paint — slightly slower roller production. Applicable to both concrete and wood substrates.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform sheen and color. No roller marks, holidays, or puddles. Even film build. Brush-cut edges invisible in final appearance. Maintain wet edge to prevent lap marks.

task_production_rates.name: Porch & Floor Enamel — Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush porch enamel on wood porch floor — used for narrow board porches, detailed areas, or when roller leaves stipple in tongue-and-groove gaps. 100 SF/hr single worker. Brush edges first, then fill field working with board direction. Slower but superior finish on wood plank floors.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform sheen and color. No brush marks visible at 3 ft. Even film build into board gaps. No drips or sags.

task_production_rates.name: Porch & Floor Enamel — Spray + Backroll
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray porch enamel onto floor surface, immediately backroll with 3/8" nap. 375 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Best for larger concrete porches and patios (>300 SF). Spray provides speed, backroll ensures even film build and eliminates texture inconsistency. Requires wind management and overspray containment.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform sheen and color. Backroll eliminates spray texture variation. No overspray on adjacent surfaces. Even wet film build verified with gauge.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Concrete Sealer — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll acrylic sealer with 3/8" nap roller on extension pole. 250 SF/hr single worker. Thin-body product flows easily — faster than porch enamel. Maintain uniform wet edge. Sealer enhances color and provides surface protection without heavy film build. Fast dry time allows same-day recoat.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform sheen — no puddles, streaks, or dry spots. Thin even coverage per TDS. No white haze from over-application. Color enhancement uniform.

task_production_rates.name: Concrete Stain — Apply and Work
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply concrete stain (acid-reactive or water-based) with pump sprayer, brush, or sponge. 200 SF/hr single worker. Acid stain is slower (reactive chemistry requires careful application and neutralization). Water-based stain is faster (wipe-on technique). Includes application, working/spreading, and any pattern manipulation.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform color depth. No puddling or uneven concentration. Acid stain properly neutralized and residue rinsed. Pattern (if any) consistent across surface.

task_production_rates.name: Polyurea Floor Coating — Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll polyurea coating with solvent-resistant roller. 275 SF/hr single worker. Two-component chemistry — mix and apply within pot life (~20-30 min). Work in manageable sections. Fast cure (walkable in 6-8 hr). Higher rate than enamel due to self-leveling properties, but limited by pot life sectioning.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete coverage with uniform film build. Mixed at correct ratio. Applied within pot life. No fisheyes, bubbles, or bare spots. Section overlap lines invisible.

task_production_rates.name: Step Detail — Tread and Riser Coating
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Coat individual porch steps — tread, riser, and nosing edge detail. 3 EA/hr (20 min per step). Includes brush-cutting nosing edges, rolling tread and riser, and feathering into floor field. Significantly slower than field work due to multiple surfaces per step and edge precision. EA from field count.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete coverage on tread, riser, and nosing. No drips at nosing edge. Even coating on all step surfaces. Color match to floor field.

task_production_rates.name: Sealer Topcoat — Final Clear Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll clear sealer topcoat over stain or as final protective layer. 250 SF/hr single worker. Same rate as acrylic sealer — thin-body, fast-flowing product. Provides UV protection, wear resistance, and locks in anti-slip aggregate. Applied after anti-slip broadcast.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform sheen. No puddles or streaks. Anti-slip aggregate fully encapsulated. No white haze from over-application.

task_production_rates.name: Anti-Slip Aggregate Broadcast — Floor Field
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Broadcast anti-slip aggregate (aluminum oxide, silica sand, or polymer grit) into wet coating on floor field. 400 SF/hr single worker. Must coordinate with final coat — broadcast into wet film before skinning. Hand-broadcast from shaker container or mechanical broadcaster. Even distribution critical for consistent texture and traction.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform aggregate distribution — no bare patches or heavy clumps. Aggregate embedded in wet film (not sitting on top). Consistent grit density across surface.

task_production_rates.name: Anti-Slip Aggregate Broadcast — Steps
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Broadcast anti-slip aggregate onto individual step treads into wet coating. 8 EA/hr (~7.5 min per step). Slower per-SF than field due to small area precision and nosing edge concentration. Extra aggregate at nosing for maximum traction at step edge. Must coordinate with step detail coating timing.

defect_tolerance.all: Aggregate on all step treads. Concentrated at nosing edge. Uniform distribution. Embedded in wet film.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Protection and Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all tape, plastic, and tarps from wall base, railing bases, thresholds, landscape, and hardscape. 25 min baseline. Pull tape at 45-degree angle to prevent edge lifting. Bag all waste. Inspect masked surfaces for any bleed-through requiring touch-up.

defect_tolerance.all: All masking removed cleanly. No tape residue on surfaces. No coating bleed-through on protected surfaces. All waste collected.

task_production_rates.name: Replace Furniture and Fixtures
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Return porch furniture, planters, rugs, and accessories to original positions after coating has cured. 30 min baseline. Use felt pads under furniture legs to protect new coating. Only after cure time per product TDS (typically 24-72 hr for foot traffic, 7 days for furniture).

defect_tolerance.all: All items returned to original or owner-specified positions. Felt pads placed under all furniture legs. No scuffs or damage to new coating during replacement.

task_production_rates.name: Final Inspection and Touch-Up
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk entire floor surface at low angle to check for holidays, thin spots, roller marks, and anti-slip aggregate uniformity. Touch up any defects. 25 min baseline includes inspection pass and minor touch-up. Not area-dependent — visual scan coverage rate is fast, touch-up is targeted.

defect_tolerance.all: No holidays, thin spots, or inconsistent texture visible at 3 ft standing height. Anti-slip aggregate uniform. Edge lines clean. Step nosing edges fully coated.

task_production_rates.name: Equipment Cleanup and Demobilization
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean rollers, brushes, spray equipment, concrete prep tools. Bag waste, load truck. 25 min baseline. Polyurea and epoxy equipment requires solvent flush (slightly longer). Dispose of acid etch neutralization waste per local code.

defect_tolerance.all: All tools cleaned and stored. Waste properly disposed. Work area clean. No materials left on site.

factor_modifiers.name: Coating System Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Coating system type affects application complexity and production rate. Porch enamel is baseline (most common residential floor coating). Acrylic sealer is faster (thin, flows easily). Concrete stain is slightly slower (reactive chemistry, pattern work). Polyurea is slowest (two-component, pot life constraints).
factor_modifiers.notes: Porch enamel is baseline (1.00x). Acrylic sealer is 10% faster (0.90x = effective rate increase) — thin body, fast dry. Concrete stain is 10% slower (1.10x) — reactive chemistry requires careful application. Polyurea is 15% slower (1.15x) — two-component mixing, pot life constraints, section management. Modifier applies to APPLICATION tasks only — prep and primer rates are substrate-driven, not coating-driven.

factor_modifiers.name: Exposure Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Covered porch vs open patio affects working conditions. Open patios require dry time management for sun exposure, dew point monitoring, and wind-related overspray containment.
factor_modifiers.notes: Covered porch is baseline (1.00x) — roof overhead protects from rain, dew, and direct sun. Open patio is 5% slower (1.05x) — must manage sun exposure on coatings (potential flash drying), monitor dew point for evening application windows, and may need wind barriers for spray operations. Minor modifier because ground-level work has inherently less environmental exposure than wall/siding work.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Direct sun on horizontal floor surfaces causes flash drying of coatings. Horizontal surfaces are more affected than vertical because full solar load hits the entire working surface simultaneously.
factor_modifiers.notes: Shade (covered porch or north exposure) is baseline. Partial sun is 5% slower. Full sun is 15% slower — horizontal surfaces absorb maximum solar radiation, concrete can exceed 130F in direct sun causing flash drying, lap marks, and reduced film build. Full sun may force early morning or late afternoon work windows only. Applies to primer and application tasks where wet film is exposed to sun.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Concrete and wood floor surface temperature affects coating cure and working time. Cold surfaces extend recoat intervals. Hot surfaces cause flash drying and coating failure.
factor_modifiers.notes: Optimal: 50-90F surface temp. Cold surface (<50F): coatings cure slower, recoat windows extend 2-3x, productivity drops 10% due to extended wait times. Hot surface (>90F): BLOCKED per SOP — floor coatings fail immediately on overheated surfaces (flash drying, bubbling, delamination). Concrete retains and radiates heat — surface temp can exceed air temp by 20-40F in direct sun.

quality_effects.description: Porch floor specs do not use traditional quality tier (QT) as primary dimension. Coating system type drives task selection, coat count, and production rate. All porch floor work is inherently QT3-equivalent — exterior floor coating is a performance-critical application where minimum standards are high.

porch_enamel.notes: Two coats of porch enamel over primer. Interstage inspection between coats. Anti-slip aggregate broadcast into wet final coat. Most common residential system.

acrylic_sealer.notes: Two coats of acrylic sealer over primer. No interstage inspection — thin film, fast dry. Anti-slip aggregate broadcast into final coat. Natural concrete appearance with protection.

concrete_stain.notes: Stain applied in 1-2 coats (acid stain typically 1, water-based typically 2) over primer. Sealer topcoat locks in color and anti-slip aggregate. Interstage inspection after stain to verify color uniformity before sealing.

polyurea.notes: Polyurea primer + basecoat + topcoat system. Anti-slip aggregate broadcast into basecoat, then sealed with topcoat. Fast cure — full system can be applied in single day. No interstage inspection — fast cure windows require continuous application.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Covered porch, concrete, porch enamel roll — best case baseline
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — covered porch, shade, optimal temp, standard enamel. 200 SF/hr single worker.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Open patio, concrete, porch enamel roll, partial sun
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Open patio with partial sun. 181 SF/hr — minor slowdown from exposure management.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Open patio, concrete, polyurea roll, full sun — worst application case
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Polyurea on open patio in full sun (assuming surface temp still in optimal range). 198 SF/hr. Note: if surface temp exceeds 90F, operation is BLOCKED. Combined modifier 1.39x — well under 4.0x cap.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Open patio, concrete, concrete stain, full sun, cold surface — maximum stacking
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Maximum stacking scenario (excluding BLOCKED conditions). Concrete stain on open patio, full sun exposure, cold surface. Combined modifier 1.46x — well under 4.0x stacking cap. 137 SF/hr is still productive.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Covered porch, wood, porch enamel brush — wood substrate baseline
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Covered wood porch, brush application. 100 SF/hr single worker. Brush is standard for wood plank porches.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Open patio, concrete, acrylic sealer roll — fastest application
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Acrylic sealer (fast coating) on open patio in shade. Effective rate exceeds base due to coating system < 1.0x. 265 SF/hr single worker.

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backroll are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + roller). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for roll and brush are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
Spray/backroll coupling rule satisfied on all spray_backroll tasks: spray component rate <= backroll component rate (same combined rate).
Substrate type (concrete vs wood) drives TASK SELECTION branching — not a rate modifier. Concrete tasks and wood tasks are separate entries with substrate-appropriate base rates.
FAC_PRFL_COATING_SYSTEM applies to APPLICATION and SEALER tasks only — prep and primer rates are substrate-driven, not coating-driven.
FAC_PRFL_EXPOSURE_TYPE applies to all primer and application tasks — both are affected by open vs covered working conditions.
FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE applies to primer and application tasks on concrete primarily — wood porch floors are almost always covered (open wood patios are rare).
FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP applies to all coating tasks — cold and hot surfaces affect all chemistries.
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (coating_system x exposure_type x sun_exposure x surface_temp).
Maximum combined modifier: 1.46x (concrete_stain 1.10 x open_patio 1.05 x full_sun 1.15 x cold_surface 1.10). Well under 4.0x stacking cap.
No height modifier — all porch/patio work is ground level.
No substrate condition modifier — NC spec (new construction, no prior coatings).
Anti-slip aggregate broadcast is MANDATORY on all porch floor coatings — safety requirement for exterior horizontal surfaces. Binary task, always included.
Step detail tasks are condition_conditional — only when porch has steps (not all do).
Moisture testing is substrate_conditional — concrete only. Wood uses pin-type MC meter (different task).
Concrete prep method (acid_etch vs diamond_grind) is coating_conditional — polyurea requires diamond grind, enamel/sealer can use either.
FIXED time tasks are not area-dependent. Porch size does not affect mobilization, furniture staging, or inspection fixed times.
Crack fill rate (30 LF/hr) is for hairline to 1/4" cracks. Wider cracks or spalls require patching at significantly lower rates — flag for estimator review.
Polyurea system requires diamond grind prep (CSP 3-5). Acid etch is insufficient for polyurea adhesion.
Furniture replacement timing is AFTER full cure — porch enamel 24-72 hr walk, 7 days furniture. Polyurea 6-8 hr walk, 24 hr furniture. Estimator must account for return visit if needed.
risks: Hot surface BLOCKED condition on open patios in summer — concrete surface temps can exceed 130F in direct sun. Project scheduling must account for early morning/late afternoon work windows only. Lost productivity from shortened work days is NOT captured in modifier (it's a scheduling constraint, not a rate modifier).
Polyurea pot life (~20-30 min) creates urgency during application. If worker pace falls behind, mixed material is wasted. Experienced applicators only — flag for crew assignment.

Acid etch waste (muriatic acid) requires neutralization and proper disposal per local environmental codes. Runoff into landscape beds or storm drains is prohibited. Additional time for containment and disposal not fully captured in base rate.

Concrete moisture testing requires 60-72 hr for results (calcium chloride method). This is a SCHEDULING constraint — project start cannot begin until results confirm moisture levels acceptable. May require separate mobilization for testing.
Concrete crack fill is cosmetic only — structural cracks (>1/4" or actively moving) require structural repair before coating. Flag for estimator review and customer disclosure.
Open patio polyurea application in wind requires containment barriers — polyurea overspray is extremely difficult to remove from adjacent surfaces.
Porch enamel on wood in direct sun can cause bubbling — gas escaping from heated wood through wet film. SOP scheduling guidance addresses this but field compliance varies.
Anti-slip aggregate density affects both safety and aesthetics. Too sparse = slip hazard. Too dense = rough/uncomfortable for bare feet. Customer expectation setting required.
Furniture replacement on fresh porch enamel — 7-day cure before heavy furniture. Customer must be informed of restricted access period. Felt pads mandatory under all furniture legs.
validation_plan: Time 3 porch enamel roll projects on concrete (covered porch) to calibrate 200 SF/hr baseline.
Time 2 porch enamel brush projects on wood plank porch to calibrate 100 SF/hr baseline.
Time 2 spray_backroll projects on concrete patios (>400 SF) to calibrate 375 SF/hr per 2-person crew.
Time 2 acrylic sealer roll projects to validate 250 SF/hr baseline and 0.90x coating system modifier.
Time 1 polyurea system project to validate 275 SF/hr roll rate and pot life management overhead.
Time 2 acid etch projects to validate 300 SF/hr baseline including neutralization and rinse.
Time 1 diamond grind project to validate 700 SF/hr equipment-assisted rate.
Track concrete crack fill time per LF by crack severity (hairline vs 1/4") to validate 30 LF/hr average.
Track step detail coating time per EA across 3 projects to validate 3 EA/hr (20 min/step) rate.
Compare covered porch vs open patio application rates on similar projects to validate 1.05x exposure modifier.
Track furniture staging and replacement times across 5 projects to validate FIXED time ranges.
Track anti-slip aggregate broadcast rate on floor field vs steps to validate SF and EA rates.
Measure actual concrete surface temperatures on open patios at different times of day to validate BLOCKED threshold guidance.
